title: Roots navigate around decay regions by sensing local pH gradients.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded the full Zenodo record listing (26 files, 352.6 MB total, CC-BY): Readme.txt, 'Updated Data S4.xlsx' (186 KB) and 24 raw LC-MS (liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry) mzML files. Opened Data S4 in pandas: 5 sheets, one per decaying substrate, with 161 (rotten apple), 219 (rotten leaf), 217 (rotten sawdust) and 395 (rotten chicken) annotated metabolite rows = 992 rows total, each with 3 replicate peak intensities, Mode/Adduct/Level/Formula/RT/PubChem CID columns. Searched NCBI GEO, SRA and BioProject for any sequencing deposit from this study (none found); confirmed the Science article itself is paywalled (HTTP 403) and has no PubMed Central record, so no data availability statement was readable.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: Everything about the biology - that roots bend away from decaying plant matter in four species, that fungal organic acids make the pH gradient, the RGF-RGFR (root meristem growth factor peptide and its receptor) sensing step, the abscisic acid asymmetry and microtubule reorganisation - comes from the abstract plus an open-access commentary in Plant Communications (PMC13589567). No root-bending angles, pH measurements, imaging data or microbiome sequencing are in any file I could reach.

a1_downloadable.note: Zenodo record 21621661 is open CC-BY and downloaded without login; I retrieved Readme.txt and the Data S4 spreadsheet directly.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: FAIL. The outcome the paper is about - root bending angle away from decay, pH gradient steepness, abscisic acid asymmetry - is in no deposited file. The only table is metabolite peak intensities; any label (e.g. 'this substrate triggers avoidance') would have to be constructed by hand from the paper's figures, and only 4 substrate categories exist.

a3_inputs_present.note: For the metabolite table the inputs are present: formula, exact mass, retention time and PubChem CID for 992 rows, so structures are resolvable without mass lookup chains.

a4_units_stated.note: FAIL (minor relative to A2/A5). Replicate columns are unlabelled raw mass-spectrometry peak areas with no unit, no normalisation statement and no shared internal standard across sheets, so abundances are not comparable between substrates.

a5_enough_rows.note: FAIL. The experimental unit is the sample: 4 substrates x 3 replicates = 12 LC-MS runs. Treating metabolites as rows gives 992 annotated compounds but with no outcome attached to them; the checklist floor is ~1,500 labelled rows (~400 for classification).

a6_fits_laptop.working_set: 0.19 MB spreadsheet; 353 MB if all 24 raw mzML files were pulled
a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits 16 GB RAM; size is not the problem here.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Cannot fully check - the Science full text is paywalled - but the Readme, the Zenodo description (four substrates: apple debris, leaf litter, sawdust, chicken tissue) and the four spreadsheet sheets agree with each other and with the commentary.

a8_label_provenance.note: FAIL. The only label-like column is the compound identity, which is a vendor library match (Metware 'MW' IDs with confidence Level 2/3 and a match 'score'), i.e. another annotation pipeline's output computed from the same m/z and retention-time features - exactly the circularity A8 warns about.

honest_claim_h3: No honest claim is possible: with 12 mass-spectrometry runs and no deposited root phenotype, any model would be describing four substrates, not a biological rule.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use the chemical profile of rotting material to predict whether a root will grow away from it.
plain_idea.train_on: Would need, per decaying substrate, its metabolite profile plus the measured root response. Only 12 profiles exist (4 substrates x 3 replicates) and 0 root-response measurements are deposited.
plain_idea.predict: Root bending angle away from the decay source, measured by imaging seedlings on agar plates and scoring tip angle - a measurement that appears only in the paper's figures, not in any file.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Soil ecologists and root biologists would like a rule for which decay chemistries repel roots, but this dataset has four substrates, which is a bar chart rather than a model.

ml_idea: The only conceivable task - predict root avoidance (yes/no) from a decaying substrate's metabolite fingerprint - has 4 distinct substrates and 12 runs behind it, and the avoidance outcome is not in the data at all. A secondary idea, predicting retention time or compound class from structure using the 992 annotated metabolites, is both a solved problem and circular, because the compound identities are themselves a matching pipeline's output.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, not timed: the spreadsheet is 186 KB and parsed in pandas in under a second; the 24 mzML files total 353 MB and would stream fine. Compute was never the constraint.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the samples in Data S4: 4 substrates x 3 replicates = 12. That alone kills it, and it took one minute.

verdict_reason: Only 12 mass-spectrometry samples are deposited (4 decaying substrates x 3 replicates, 992 annotated metabolite rows with unlabelled raw peak areas), and the paper's actual outcome - root bending away from decay, the pH gradients, the imaging - is not in any public file. A2 fails because the label would have to be built from the figures, A5 fails on sample count, A4 fails on missing intensity units, and A8 fails because the compound identities are a vendor annotation pipeline's output. The biology is lovely and the Zenodo deposit is clean and openly licensed; it is simply a metabolomics supplement, not an ML dataset.
